features.feature_value: Used tone/respectfulness (e.g., cursing, mudslinging, unproductive argument) to justify evaluation and moderation.
features.evidence_span: Bad grammar, illogical thoughts, cursing, and unproductive mudslinging
features.rationale: The participant explicitly ties cursing/mudslinging and lack of respect to how they evaluated posts.

features.feature_value: Removed both when speech was inflammatory or included cursing (treated as a trigger).
features.evidence_span: If the statements were inflammatory... I chose to remove both posts... If there was cursing, I chose to remove both posts
features.rationale: They state a direct rule linking inflammatory wording/cursing to removing both versions.

features.feature_value: Only removes if content calls for violence.
features.evidence_span: I only really would remove them if any called for violence
features.rationale: They clearly identify violence calls as the condition for removal.

features.feature_value: Default to leave up; remove only when profanity or violence is present (and only one pair due to profanity).
features.evidence_span: My default position is leave them all up unless they are profane or promote violence
features.rationale: They state an explicit default rule with exceptions tied to profanity/violence.

features.feature_value: Even when disagreeing with political side, tone cues (profanity, anger, leaning toward violent wording) determined permit vs remove for both.
features.evidence_span: made my decisions based on the tone of what was posted... word(profane) choices and how angry(leaning toward violent) wording
features.rationale: They describe using tone-related features to decide whether to allow/discard both posts.

features.feature_value: If they agree with one opinion, they feel they should not remove the other; removes only if both are harmful (e.g., racism/ablelism).
features.evidence_span: If I agreed to one, then I don't think I have the right to remove the other opinion
features.rationale: They articulate a symmetry rule between paired opinions and a harmfulness threshold.

features.feature_value: Evaluated whether content was a fair stance rather than an emotional reaction.
features.evidence_span: content seemed like a fair stance rather than just a reaction to pure emotion
features.rationale: They define a criterion contrasting fair stance versus pure emotionality.
